\subsection{1) Download the Sample RNA-seq Count Matrix and associated
Metadata.}\label{download-the-sample-rna-seq-count-matrix-and-associated-metadata.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Read in both data sets}
\NormalTok{count.df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{read.csv}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{file =} \StringTok{"data/counts.csv"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{header =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{meta\_data.df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{read.csv}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{file =} \StringTok{"data/meta\_data.csv"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{header =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsubsection{Data wrangling over the next sequence of
steps}\label{data-wrangling-over-the-next-sequence-of-steps}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Use only 5 columns of data in the meta\_data dataframe to make processing faster}
\NormalTok{metadata.modified }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ meta\_data.df }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
\NormalTok{  dplyr}\SpecialCharTok{::}\FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{23}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{29}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{41}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{86}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \CommentTok{\# The barcode variable will eventually be used to join the metadata to the count data}
  \CommentTok{\# The hyphen in the barcode variable needs to be changed to a dot}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{barcode =} \FunctionTok{str\_replace\_all}\NormalTok{(barcode, }\StringTok{"{-}"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"."}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Convert count.df to long format}
\CommentTok{\# This is required for many of the ggplot graphs and many other functions in R}
\CommentTok{\# Use the pivot\_longer function to convert the count dataframe to one I am calling}
\CommentTok{\# dat.long which will end up containing three columns {-} the Ensembl ID, one called}
\CommentTok{\# Samples which will contain all of the individual sample values and one called}
\CommentTok{\# Counts which will contain the gene\_expression count values}

\NormalTok{dat.long }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ count.df }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{pivot\_longer}\NormalTok{(}
    \AttributeTok{cols =} \SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{X,        }\CommentTok{\# Pivot all columns except the one containing the Ensemble ID}
    \AttributeTok{names\_to =} \StringTok{"Samples"}\NormalTok{,    }\CommentTok{\# Column name for your old wide headers}
    \AttributeTok{values\_to =} \StringTok{"Counts"}    \CommentTok{\# Column name for your data values}
\NormalTok{  )}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# This code block is where I join the dat.long dataframe for the counts to the }
\CommentTok{\# metadata dataframe for the additional information needed for the assignment}
\CommentTok{\# The results of the join are stored in a new dataframe.}
\CommentTok{\# dat.long$Samples is joined on metadata.modified$barcode}
\NormalTok{dat.long.enriched }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ dat.long }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{X =} \FunctionTok{sub}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\SpecialCharTok{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}}\StringTok{.[\^{}.]*$"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{""}\NormalTok{, X)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} \CommentTok{\# Strip off version number}
  \FunctionTok{inner\_join}\NormalTok{(., metadata.modified, }\AttributeTok{by =} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Samples"} \OtherTok{=} \StringTok{"barcode"}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# This code block is used to map the Ensembl IDs to their actual gene symbol.}

\CommentTok{\# Load required libraries}
\FunctionTok{library}\NormalTok{(AnnotationDbi) }\CommentTok{\# provides an R interface to query SQLite{-}based biological }
                       \CommentTok{\# annotation database}
\FunctionTok{library}\NormalTok{(org.Hs.eg.db)  }\CommentTok{\# Used to access genome{-}wide human annotations based primarily on }
                       \CommentTok{\# Entrez Gene identifiers}

\CommentTok{\# The Ensemble ID has a "version" number on it that needs to be stripped off because}
\CommentTok{\# the gene\_symbols generated do not have it.}
\NormalTok{count.df.mod }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ count.df }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{X =} \FunctionTok{sub}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\SpecialCharTok{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}}\StringTok{.[\^{}.]*$"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{""}\NormalTok{, X))}

\CommentTok{\# Now need to pull the processed Ensemble ID\textquotesingle{}s out into a vector}
\NormalTok{ensembl.ids }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ count.df.mod }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} \FunctionTok{pull}\NormalTok{(X)}

\CommentTok{\# This is the heart of the process where the Ensemble ID is mapped to Gene Symbols}
\CommentTok{\# Uses he mapIds() function from AnnotationDbi. Maps identifiers for genomic data by }
\CommentTok{\# connecting a set of input keys to target columns using annotation databases}
\NormalTok{gene\_symbols }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{mapIds}\NormalTok{(}
  \AttributeTok{x =}\NormalTok{ org.Hs.eg.db,}
  \AttributeTok{keys =}\NormalTok{ ensembl.ids,}
  \AttributeTok{keytype =} \StringTok{"ENSEMBL"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{column =} \StringTok{"SYMBOL"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{multiVals =} \StringTok{"first"} \CommentTok{\# Keeps the first match if duplicate mappings occur}
\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Store the results in a dataframe "df" for use in a following join operation}
\NormalTok{df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{data.frame}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{names}\NormalTok{(gene\_symbols),gene\_symbols)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# This is where I merge the previously created dataframe "df" that contains the}
\CommentTok{\# actual mapping from Ensembl ID to gene using an inner join}
\NormalTok{dat.long.genes }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ dat.long.enriched }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{inner\_join}\NormalTok{(., df, }\AttributeTok{by =} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"X"} \OtherTok{=} \StringTok{"names.gene\_symbols."}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

All of the data wrangling has been completed up to this point.
Additional steps will be required when we create the heat map

\subsection{2) Gene selection and Summary
Statistics}\label{gene-selection-and-summary-statistics}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# I am choosing the gene BRCA1 to study}
\CommentTok{\# BRCA1 is a human tumor suppressor genes that normally produce proteins to repair damaged }
\CommentTok{\# DNA and prevent uncontrolled cell growth}

\NormalTok{get\_mode }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ControlFlowTok{function}\NormalTok{(x) \{}
\NormalTok{  uniq\_x }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{unique}\NormalTok{(x)}
\NormalTok{  uniq\_x[}\FunctionTok{which.max}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{tabulate}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{match}\NormalTok{(x, uniq\_x)))]}
\NormalTok{\}}

\CommentTok{\# Using dplyr filter out only BRCA1 and do summary statistics}
\NormalTok{summary\_stats }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ dat.long.genes }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(gene\_symbols }\SpecialCharTok{==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}BRCA1\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{summarize}\NormalTok{(}
    \AttributeTok{mean =} \FunctionTok{mean}\NormalTok{(Counts, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{),}
    \AttributeTok{min =} \FunctionTok{min}\NormalTok{(Counts, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{),}
    \AttributeTok{max =} \FunctionTok{max}\NormalTok{(Counts, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{),}
    \AttributeTok{median =} \FunctionTok{median}\NormalTok{(Counts, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{),}
    \AttributeTok{mode =} \FunctionTok{get\_mode}\NormalTok{(Counts),}
    \AttributeTok{sd =} \FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(Counts, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{  )}

\NormalTok{summary\_stats}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{3) Visualization}\label{visualization}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# a) Create a Histogram: Use ggplot2 to generate a histogram of the count data for the selected gene.}
\CommentTok{\# This visualization should effectively display the distribution of the counts.}

\CommentTok{\# Using dplyr, filter for the BRCA1 gene and use the ajcc\_pathologic\_stage as fill aesthetic.}
\CommentTok{\# The ajcc\_pathologic\_stage is a standardized cancer classification assigned after a }
\CommentTok{\# patient undergoes surgical resection of the primary tumor.}
\CommentTok{\# Generate a histogram using geom\_histogram from ggplot2()}

\CommentTok{\#png("images/Distribution of BRCA1 Counts.png",}
\CommentTok{\#        width = 800, height = 600, res = 100)}

\NormalTok{dat.long.genes }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(gene\_symbols }\SpecialCharTok{==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}BRCA1\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{ggplot}\NormalTok{(., }\FunctionTok{aes}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{x=}\NormalTok{Counts)) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
    \FunctionTok{geom\_histogram}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{alpha =} \FloatTok{0.5}\NormalTok{, }
                   \AttributeTok{fill =} \StringTok{"blue"}\NormalTok{, }
                   \AttributeTok{binwidth =} \DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{,}
                   \AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
     \FunctionTok{labs}\NormalTok{(}
        \AttributeTok{title =} \StringTok{"Distribution of BRCA1 Counts"}\NormalTok{,}
        \AttributeTok{x =} \StringTok{"BRCA1 RNA{-}Sequencing Counts"}\NormalTok{,}
        \AttributeTok{y =} \StringTok{"Count of Samples"}
\NormalTok{     ) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
     \FunctionTok{theme\_minimal}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{+} 
     \FunctionTok{theme}\NormalTok{(}
       \AttributeTok{plot.title =} \FunctionTok{element\_text}\NormalTok{(}
         \AttributeTok{face =} \StringTok{"bold"}\NormalTok{,}
         \AttributeTok{hjust =} \FloatTok{0.5}
\NormalTok{       )}
\NormalTok{     )  }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

        \AttributeTok{width =} \DecValTok{800}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{height =} \DecValTok{600}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{res =} \DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# c) Create a Violin Plot: Select one covariate from your metadata. Using the count data from }

\subsubsection{New Heatmap}\label{new-heatmap}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{heatmap\_colors }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{colorRamp2}\NormalTok{(}
  \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{),}
  \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"\#2166AC"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"white"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"\#B2182B"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Define color schemes for all annotations}
\NormalTok{colour\_list }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{list}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  laterality }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Left"} \OtherTok{=} \StringTok{"blue"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Right"} \OtherTok{=} \StringTok{"orange"}\NormalTok{)}
  \CommentTok{\#sample\_type = col2rgb(unname(c("Primary Tumor" = "red", "Solid Tissue Normal" = "green"))),}
  \CommentTok{\#treatment\_method = col2rgb(unname(c("Adjuvant" = "white", "Anastrozole" = "red",}
  \CommentTok{\#                     "Carboplatin" = "green", "First{-}Line Therapy" = "blue")))}
\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Create top annotation for continuous variables}
\NormalTok{top\_ann }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{HeatmapAnnotation}\NormalTok{(}
  \AttributeTok{Laterality =}\NormalTok{ meta\_data.df.corrected\_2}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{laterality,}
  \AttributeTok{Sample\_type =}\NormalTok{ meta\_data.df.corrected\_2}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sample\_type,}
  
  \AttributeTok{annotation\_name\_gp =} \FunctionTok{gpar}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{fontsize =} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{),}
  \AttributeTok{annotation\_legend\_param =} \FunctionTok{list}\NormalTok{(}
    \AttributeTok{Laterality =} \FunctionTok{list}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{title =} \StringTok{"Laterality"}\NormalTok{),}
    \AttributeTok{Sample\_type =} \FunctionTok{list}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{title =} \StringTok{"Sample Type"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{  )}
  \CommentTok{\#colour\_list = list(laterality = Laterality)}
\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Create bottom annotation for treatment variables}
\NormalTok{bottom\_ann }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{HeatmapAnnotation}\NormalTok{(}
  \AttributeTok{Treatment\_Method =}\NormalTok{ meta\_data.df.corrected\_2}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{treatment\_method,}

  \AttributeTok{annotation\_name\_gp =} \FunctionTok{gpar}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{fontsize =} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{)}
 
\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Heatmap with annotations}
\NormalTok{annotated\_heatmap }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{Heatmap}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  count.df.matrix,}
  \AttributeTok{name =} \StringTok{"Expression"}\NormalTok{,}
  
  \CommentTok{\#col = colour\_list,}
  \CommentTok{\# Clustering parameters}
  \AttributeTok{clustering\_distance\_rows =} \StringTok{"spearman"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{clustering\_method\_rows =} \StringTok{"ward.D2"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{clustering\_distance\_columns =} \StringTok{"spearman"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{clustering\_method\_columns =} \StringTok{"ward.D2"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{column\_split =}\NormalTok{ meta\_data.df.corrected\_2}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{treatment\_method,}
  
  \AttributeTok{top\_annotation =}\NormalTok{ top\_ann,}
  \AttributeTok{bottom\_annotation =}\NormalTok{ bottom\_ann,}
  
  
  \AttributeTok{show\_row\_names =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{row\_names\_side =} \StringTok{"left"}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{row\_names\_gp =} \FunctionTok{gpar}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{fontsize =} \DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{),}
  \AttributeTok{show\_column\_names =} \ConstantTok{FALSE}\NormalTok{,}
  \AttributeTok{column\_names\_gp =} \FunctionTok{gpar}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{fontsize =} \DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{),}
  
  \AttributeTok{column\_title =} \StringTok{"Gene Expression"}
\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}
